question: The HCF and the LCM of two numbers are 13 and 1170, respectively. If one of the numbers is 130, find the other one.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The product of two numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM.

Second Number = (HCF × LCM) ÷ First Number

Second Number = (13 × 1170) ÷ 130

Second Number = 1170 ÷ 10 = 117

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF = 13

LCM = 1170

First Number = 130

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = HCF × LCM

 
 Product of Numbers
 130 × x
 
 =

 
 HCF × LCM
 13 × 1170
 
 
 x = 117

**Calculations:**

⇒ 130 × Second Number = 13 × 1170

⇒ Second Number = (13 × 1170) ÷ 130

⇒ Second Number = 1170 ÷ 10

⇒ Second Number = 117

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators) | LCM = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their product.

Divisibility Property

The HCF of any set of numbers is always a factor of their LCM. The LCM is always a multiple of the HCF.
